flawed_step: After matching vertices of equal degree, the attempted proof would need to infer that this bijection preserves adjacency. That inference is unjustified: degrees record only the number of neighbors, not which vertices are neighbors.
counterexample: Let G have vertices {1,2,3,4,5,6} and edges {12,23,34,45,56,61}, so G is the 6-cycle C6. Let H have the same vertex set and edges {12,23,31,45,56,64}, so H is the disjoint union of two triangles. Every vertex in both graphs has degree 2, so both have degree sequence {2,2,2,2,2,2}. However, G is connected while H has two connected components. Isomorphisms preserve connectedness, so G and H are not isomorphic.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. Equal degree sequences allow vertices to be matched by degree but do not determine the adjacency structure; C6 and two disjoint triangles provide an explicit counterexample.
